title: The execution context bounds one session at a time, and the workspace runs three
decision: design retained, proposed ADR 0031 drafted for human review, no production change
code_state: no file under crates/ was modified by this batch
reason_codes: item CORE-3 of change 0587 names the gap from the source; this record measures it and finds the mechanism is not pool duplication but that ExecutionLimits::workers is a per-session Copy value while Budget is the only shared part of an ExecutionContext, so the missing budgets must be hierarchical Resource dimensions rather than more policy fields

the design amends the execution paragraph of accepted ADR 0005, so docs/GOAL.md line 80 applies: the conflict is recorded and a separate proposed ADR is drafted for human review rather than implemented
no end-to-end scenario admits even one of the three sessions today, so completing the execution context is a prerequisite for work that does not yet exist and no speedup is available to claim

the retained scaling evidence across changes 0009, 0088, 0405, 0498 and 0499 is that width helps only for few-and-large independent work, hurts for many-and-small, and that every apparent scheduler win has been withdrawn or fenced by its own record; the admission gates in section 7 are written against that evidence

accepted_evidence.capability_matrix: the seven docs/GOAL.md Workstream F capabilities against litchi_core::ExecutionLimits, ExecutionContext and Budget at 1e4198321, with the file and line of each present capability and the absence of the other three verified by grep
accepted_evidence.parallel_site_census: the three production parallel sessions, with every other rayon, thread::scope, spawn_scoped and thread::spawn under crates/ verified to be test code; zero callers of read_parts_ordered, bulk_read and OpenSession outside litchi-opc, litchi-cfb, their own tests, one example and the harness
accepted_evidence.coexistence_counts: live OS threads from /proc/self/task at each stage and sampled from inside a worker's own read_at, plus simultaneous ReadAt::read_at calls, at workers 1, 2, 4 and 8, five repeats per width; every thread count identical across all five repeats
accepted_evidence.retained_scaling: changes 0009 (widths 1/2/4/8/12, speedup, efficiency and Amdahl serial fraction for OPC and CFB few-large and many-small), 0498 (six corpus/source rows at serial and batch 1/4/8), 0499 (worker reuse deltas and the residual parallel-versus-serial gap), 0088 (no accepted speedup across 62 cells) and 0240 and 0405 (what the harness may and may not say about parallelism)
accepted_evidence.cost_pricing: 589 Limits::new call sites across 234 files under crates/ and 22 under tools/, RESOURCE_COUNT 6, and 14 match sites naming Resource::Depth as an arm, which is why proposed ADR 0031 makes the three new dimensions additive rather than positional

accepted_costs.instrument: the 500 microsecond fixed per-read delay is a deterministic test instrument that widens the observation window for concurrent reads; it models no production storage, scheduler, allocator or decompression latency, in the same role change 0088's fixed 10 ms source delay plays
accepted_costs.synthetic_corpora: the probe uses an in-memory four-member OPC archive and a four-stream CFB file, one MiB each; it measures the structure of the three sessions, not any real document workload
accepted_costs.single_host_single_platform: counts taken on one Linux host reading /proc/self/task, pinned with taskset -c 10 while eight agents built concurrently; nothing here says what a macOS or Windows runtime adapter would report
accepted_costs.process_concurrency_is_a_lower_bound: the process-wide concurrent-read figure is the largest overlap two independently scheduled sessions happened to achieve in a run, not a proof of the maximum reachable; it reached the arithmetic sum of the per-session maxima in three of five repeats at widths 4 and 8
accepted_costs.retained_not_remeasured: every scaling figure in section 4 comes from changes 0009, 0498 and 0499, taken on different hosts, corpora and tree states; their own out-of-model caveats are reproduced rather than dropped

known_gaps.no_timing: no timing leg, no A/B or A/A pair, no allocation or RSS profile, no callgrind run and no harness capture was taken in this batch
known_gaps.no_consumer: no format crate or facade path reaches any of the three sessions, so there is no end-to-end scenario against which the design could be measured; item CORE-4 / SAVE-6 is the most likely first real consumer and needs its own frozen design
known_gaps.profile_values: proposed ADR 0031 requires finite Workers, IoConcurrency and CpuTasks values for Profile::Server, Profile::Desktop and Profile::TrustedBatch, and deliberately leaves the three numbers to the reviewer
known_gaps.unimplemented_free_win: gate G1, making ParallelReadSession build its pool lazily as SharedOleBulkRead already does, needs no ADR and is not implemented here either; this batch's scope is documentation plus the probe

withheld: any speedup, regression, latency, tail, peak-RSS, allocation, cold-cache, physical-device, range-source, scaling, contention, lock-wait, cross-platform or real-producer result
any authority for proposed ADR 0031: it is not accepted, is absent from the accepted table in docs/adr/README.md, and no code may cite it until a human accepts it

provenance.note: the probe is a separate Cargo project with path dependencies on this worktree's crates, built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the repository; its working copy and target directory were deleted after the runs and its source is retained verbatim in probe/
